source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:35 ('כי לוא אוכל לקום — one of TWO in the Torah full with vav and aleph; its companion is If-he-does-NOT-tell of Vayikra; so the Ramah') + Kitzur 31:35 (the halakhic pairing: she cannot rise BEFORE YOU — as the witness who does not tell bears guilt only toward the claimant)
claim_en: THE TWO FULL NOS: לוא ('I canNOT rise before you,' 31:35 — Rachel seated on the hidden idols) is written with both vav and aleph exactly twice in the Torah, and its one companion is the oath-witness law: 'if he does NOT tell, he bears his guilt' (Lev 5:1). The Kitzur reads the pair as one rule — her not-rising is only 'before YOU,' as the silent witness's guilt is only toward the claimant: the Torah's two overfull refusals, spelled for each other.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's pair; the Kitzur's one-rule reading, E7, rides beside)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:31 ('בנותיך — full in all the books and the Yerushalmi against the Hilleli's lean; ONE of three full in the whole Bible per the Masorah, and the Torah's only one — the Ramah: every like-form in the Torah is lean of vav except this one, full of full, its sign: lest-you-TEAR-away')
claim_en: THE ONE FULL DAUGHTERS: בנותיך ('for I said, lest you TEAR YOUR DAUGHTERS from me,' 31:31 — Jacob's one confession of the fear behind the flight) is the Torah's ONE daughters-of-yours written full with both vav and yod; its two lean twins (builder-checked) are Lot's daughters at doomed Sodom (19:15) and the wage-ledger's 'fourteen years for your two daughters' (31:41). The word is whole only where the father fears it torn.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:47 ('יגר שהדותא — Rabbeinu Gershom's book wrote it with SAMEKH, reasoning from the Masorah's written-shin-read-samekh list; a great error — the Torah's language is its own and Aramaic is its own, and the Aramaic-translation samekh may not be forced back onto the letter of the Torah')
claim_en: THE ARAMAIC WITNESS IN HEBREW LETTERS: שהדותא ('the HEAP OF WITNESS' — Laban's Aramaic name for the mound, the Torah's one Aramaic naming) is written with the letter shin (pointed sin, the s-sound), NOT the samekh of the Targum's own spelling — Minchat Shai overruling Rabbeinu Gershom's samekh: even speaking Laban's tongue, the letter keeps the Torah's own alphabet. SNAPSHOT carries the shin.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:45 ('וירימה — full yod in the Hilleli and all our books, the Masorah marking NONE LIKE IT; the Yerushalmi's lean form — the Ramah: the lean reading is an error, the precise copies agree with the first Masorah')
claim_en: THE STONE RAISED FULL: וירימה ('and Jacob took a stone AND RAISED IT as a pillar,' 31:45) — written full with its yod, the Masorah marking it none-like-it, with the Hilleli, all the precise books, and the Ramah's arbitration against the Yerushalmi's lean form: the witness-pillar's raising written whole.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 31:22 ('כי ברח — 2 in the Masorah: that Jacob FLED, that the people FLED (Exod 14:5); the midrash: AMALEK told Laban of Jacob's flight, and told Pharaoh of Israel's; and כי ברח in gematria is עמלק')
claim_en: THE TWO TOLD FLIGHTS: the Masorah pairs the flight-word followed by the fleer's name exactly twice — 'it was told to Laban... that JACOB fled' (31:22) and 'it was told to the king of Egypt that THE PEOPLE fled' (Exod 14:5): the ancestor's flight and the nation's, each betrayed by a telling. The midrash names the teller both times as AMALEK — and the letters of כי ברח ('that he fled') sum to 240, the count of עמלק itself (builder-checked): the informer signed inside the phrase.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the two told flights; the informer's letter-sum, E29, rides beside)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 31:33 ('מאהל — 4 in the Masorah: he went out FROM THE TENT of Leah; FROM THE TENT of meeting; I have walked from tent to tent (I Chr 17:5); He tears you from the tent (Ps 52:7) — the Rosh: the altar-history of the tents, from Bezalel of Leah's line to Shiloh in Joseph's portion')
claim_en: FROM-THE-TENT, TWICE IN THE TORAH: מאהל stands exactly twice in the Torah — Laban going out FROM THE TENT of Leah empty-handed (31:33) and the Voice calling to Moses FROM THE TENT of meeting (Lev 1:1); the Masorah's other two members stand in Chronicles and Psalms, named. The Kitzur carries the Rosh's reading: the search-tent of Leah and the meeting-tent are one thread — the Tabernacle's builder Bezalel rising from Leah's line.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:30 ('גנבת — the gimel SOFT')
claim_en: THE ACCUSATION SOFT: גנבת ('why did you STEAL my gods?', 31:30 — Laban's charge against Jacob) — the gimel soft, no doubling dot, exactly as ruled.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:32 ('גנבתם — the gimel DAGESHED and the tav in patach')
claim_en: AND THE DEED DAGESHED: גנבתם ('and Jacob did not know that Rachel HAD STOLEN THEM,' 31:32 — the narrator's fact under Jacob's death-sentence oath) — the gimel dageshed and the tav in patach as ruled: Laban's soft-gimel charge (31:30) answered two verses later by the hard-gimel deed, the doubling dot marking where the theft actually lives.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:39 ('גנבתי — the nun ought by form to carry shuruk; the three-dot short vowel WITH THE MAARICH stands in the place of the long one, and the sheva after it is mobile — the rule of all such shortened forms, as R. Solomon of Acre wrote to me; I have set it out at length in my Essay of the Maarich')
claim_en: THE STOLEN-BY-DAY WORD AND THE METEG LAW: גנבתי ('the STOLEN of day and the stolen of night,' 31:39 — Jacob's shepherd-oath) — the nun carries the three-dot short u WITH the meteg (the small stress-stroke) exactly as Minchat Shai's own maarich-law requires: the short vowel with the stroke standing in for the long shuruk the form calls for. His essay's rule, present in the stream point for point.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:26 + 31:28 + 31:43 ('בנתי — lean of vav; so the Ramah; and every like-form lean')
claim_en: MY-DAUGHTERS ALWAYS LEAN: בנתי ('you led away MY DAUGHTERS like captives of the sword,' 31:26) — lean of its vav as the Ramah rules, and the leanness holds through every token of Laban's my-daughters in the unit: the kiss he was denied (31:28), the everything-is-mine claim's two (31:43), and both tokens of the covenant's protection-clause (31:50), builder-checked one by one — six lean writes against the ONE full daughters-of-yours in Jacob's mouth (31:31).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:27 ('בשמחה ובשרים — this one ALONE of the Torah's song-language is lean of its first yod')
claim_en: THE ONE LEAN SONG: ובשרים ('I would have sent you away with joy AND WITH SONGS,' 31:27 — Laban's counterfactual farewell) — of all the Torah's song-language, this token alone is written lean of its first yod: the songs that were never going to be sung, spelled one letter short of song.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:36 ('מה פשעי מה חטאתי — some old books wrote the second with vav, and hands erased and restored it; but from the Masorah's mouth we know it is WITHOUT vav: the Exodus list counts the verses of double-what, four in the Torah and four in the Prophets and Writings, and this is one; so the Ramah')
claim_en: WHAT AND WHAT, UNJOINED: מה חטאתי ('WHAT is my transgression, WHAT is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?', 31:36) — the second what stands bare, no joining vav, exactly as the Masorah's double-what list rules against the wavering old books: Jacob's two questions hammered separately, not chained.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:41 ('ותחלף — the lamed in TZERE; Chizkuni')
claim_en: THE WAGE-CHANGE IN THE LONG E: ותחלף ('and you CHANGED my wage ten counts,' 31:41 — the ledger restated at the confrontation) — the lamed in tzere as Chizkuni rules: the change-verb of 31:7 returning with its vowel held long.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:42 ('לולי — written with YOD in the books of Rabbeinu Gershom and R. Yehudah; so the Ramah arbitrated')
claim_en: UNLESS, WITH THE YOD: לולי ('UNLESS the God of my father... had been for me,' 31:42 — the speech's pivot to heaven) — written with its closing yod per Rabbeinu Gershom's and R. Yehudah's books and the Ramah's arbitration, against the aleph-form that stands elsewhere.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:44 ('ועתה — with REVIA, not zaqef gadol')
claim_en: AND-NOW UNDER REVIA: ועתה ('AND NOW, come, let us cut a covenant,' 31:44 — Laban's turn from quarrel to treaty) — carrying revia (the pausing four-dot accent), not the zaqef gadol of the other camp, exactly as ruled.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:50 ('תענה — the nun in SEGOL in all the precise manuscripts; Or Torah weighed the divided Masorot, and the resolution stands: if-you-AFFLICT my daughters (here) in segol, the doubled afflict-afflict of Mishpatim in tzere')
claim_en: IF-YOU-AFFLICT, IN SEGOL: תענה ('IF YOU AFFLICT my daughters... God is witness,' 31:50 — the covenant's protection clause) — the nun in segol (the short e) with all the precise manuscripts, the divided Masorot resolved exactly this way: segol for the daughters' clause here, tzere reserved for the doubled affliction-warning of the widow-and-orphan law (Exod 22:22), named.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:52 ('אני — the aleph in qamatz though not at a pause, and MILEIL — stressed on the first syllable; the Michlol lists its like')
claim_en: THE OATH'S STRESSED I: אני ('if I do not cross this heap to you,' 31:52) — the aleph in qamatz with the accent sitting ON the aleph itself: stressed mileil (front-stressed) exactly as ruled, the self-binding pronoun leaning on its first letter.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:52 ('ואם אתה — end-stressed, carrying only the telisha, which always sits at the head of the word and does not shift the stress; so the books of Spain with ONE telisha alone; some old and printed copies set TWO telishas to signal the stress')
claim_en: AND-IF-YOU WITH THE SINGLE TELISHA: אתה ('and if YOU do not cross to me,' 31:52) — one telisha gedola (the detached flourish-accent) at the word's head and nothing more, exactly the books of Spain's camp against the copies that doubled the mark to signal the end-stress: SNAPSHOT carries the Sephardic single stroke.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 31:53 ('אלהי אברהם ואלהי נחור... אלהי אביהם — tractate Soferim ch. 4: the God of Abraham HOLY, the god of Nahor PROFANE, the god of their-father PROFANE; so Rashi. Bereshit Rabbah: their-father carries BOTH senses — holy and profane — read on Terah who served idols and repented') + 31:29 ('יש לאל ידי — this אל is PROFANE per Soferim ch. 4')
claim_en: THE ORACLE'S HOLY AND PROFANE NAMES (classification layer, uninstrumented): the double invocation 'the God of Abraham and the god of Nahor... the god of their father' (31:53) — Soferim rules Abraham's holy, Nahor's profane, their-father's profane; Bereshit Rabbah reads their-father's as BOTH, on Terah's repentance; and the power-word אל of 'it is in the power of my hand' (31:29) is likewise ruled profane. SNAPSHOT's stream does not carry the holy/profane classification — the layer's station count grows to eight, filed unsettled.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:12
claim_en: THE SWEEP'S CROWN DOCTRINE: LABOUR OUTRANKS INHERITED MERIT. The chain first states a rule about a particular conditional word - wherever it appears, the merit of the fathers is meant - records the objection from a verse where it plainly is not, and harmonizes. Then at 31:42 it mints the doctrine outright: labour is MORE BELOVED than the merit of the fathers, because merit salvaged only money while labour saved lives - read off the verse's own pairing of the fathers' God with 'my hardship and the toil of my hands God saw'. A wage-earner's toil ranked above inherited standing, at the verse where a wage dispute is being argued.

check.note: Inherited merit explicitly ranked below personal labour, argued from one verse's pairing of both terms.

middah: plain (labour more beloved than the fathers' merit — read off the verse's pairing; the conditional-word rule, M-09, beside)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:12
claim_en: THE CHAIN AUDITS ITS OWN TRANSMISSION IN THE SAME BREATH. Reporting the rule about the conditional word, R. Tanchuma adds a note that some invert which sage said which opinion - the attribution recorded as uncertain rather than smoothed. A record that flags its own provenance doubt at the point of transmission.

check.note: An attribution explicitly flagged as disputed by the transmitter within the same passage.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:7; Onkelos Genesis 31:24
claim_en: THE GENTILE-PROPHECY GUARD IS STATED AND RENDERED AT ONE VERSE. The doctrine holds that the nations' prophets receive only truncated speech and only at night, like a king's friend behind a curtain - and the ink is made to carry it, the verse using the shortened verb. Onkelos enforces the same guard grammatically: God does not visit the man, but A WORD CAME FROM BEFORE THE LORD to him. Exposition and translation at one door, the third instance of this pattern in the derived corpus after 20:3 and 24:63.

check.note: A prophecy-grade doctrine stated by the midrash and enforced grammatically by the translation at the same verse.

middah: plain (the gentile-prophecy guard; the shortened verb an ink point; Onkelos's word-from-before)

source: Onkelos Genesis 31:39
claim_en: THE SHEPHERD'S COMPLAINT IS RECAST IN THE VOCABULARY OF THE BAILMENT LAWS. Where the verse has a poetic defence - I bore its loss, from my hand you demanded it, stolen by day or by night - Onkelos writes the custody-law terms: that which was MISSING FROM THE COUNT you demanded from my hand; I GUARDED by day and I GUARDED by night. The count, the demand and the watch are the operative terms of the keeper statutes, so the translation files a narrative grievance under the law of bailment. This is the clearest law-wire yet from a narrative block into the ordinances the case-file machinery will need.

check.note: A narrative grievance re-rendered in the operative vocabulary of the keeper statutes.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

source: Onkelos Genesis 31:49; Onkelos Genesis 31:50
claim_en: THE PACT IS NOTARIZED BY THE WORD. Both the watching and the witnessing of the covenant are routed through the Memra - the WORD of the LORD will watch between us, the WORD of the LORD is witness - so that the buffer takes on a juridical office rather than a reverential one. Its first such office in the derived corpus: elsewhere the Word supports, promises and is sworn by; here it witnesses and watches a contract between two parties.

check.note: The reverence buffer given a juridical role as watcher and witness of a covenant, distinct from its usual functions.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:14
claim_en: THE CHAIN HONOURS THE TRANSLATION'S OWN LANGUAGE, EXACTLY WHERE THE TEXT GOES BILINGUAL. At the verse where the monument receives two names in two languages, the chain says: let this tongue not be light in your eyes - in the Torah, in the Prophets and in the Writings the Holy One pays it honour, naming a verse from each. The declared reading's translation-member is defended by its midrash-member at the one verse where the corpus itself switches language. And Onkelos leaves both names untranslated, keeping the bilingual monument bilingual.

check.note: One member of the declared reading defending the other's language, at the verse where the text itself is bilingual.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:14
claim_en: THE TREATY'S CLAUSES ARE READ AS FAMILY LAW WITH A TEMPORAL REACH. Afflicting the daughters is read as taking no other wives IN THEIR LIFETIME, and taking wives beside them as not even AFTER THEIR DEATH - the two clauses covering the two periods between them. The invocation is then read as the enforcement mechanism: God is witness where no man is. And the watchtower's name is parsed as mutual blindness - until now we saw one another, from now neither sees the other.

check.note: Two treaty clauses read as partitioning time before and after death, with a witness clause as the enforcement term.

middah: plain (afflict and take-beside read as the two periods — in their lifetime, after their death)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:15
claim_en: THE BOUNDARY PACT IS ARGUED IN COURT CENTURIES LATER AS A LIVE INSTRUMENT. The treaty carries a commerce carve-out - you shall not pass for HARM, but you may pass for TRADE - and the chain then records its legal afterlife: nations producing their standing epistles when a general reaches their borders, and a king removing crown and purple to argue the breaches before the high court rather than by force. The letter-count is disputed and a casualty discrepancy reconciled as two separate wars. A narrative covenant treated as a document with precedential force.

check.note: A narrative treaty carried forward as an operative document argued before a court, with its carve-out and disputes recorded.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:16; Onkelos Genesis 31:53
claim_en: ONE OATH FORMULA IS SPLIT BY REGISTER, WORD BY WORD. The invocation names three parties, and the chain grades them separately: one name sacred, one profane, and the third phrase carrying both senses at once. Onkelos keeps the split and unpacks the epithet into a clause - He WHOM his father feared - de-reifying the reverence term while retaining the plural verb over the mixed invocation. The verse's own two-tier theology is adjudicated term by term rather than resolved.

check.note: A single oath formula graded sacred, profane and ambiguous word by word, with the translation preserving the split.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:10
claim_en: THE QUARREL IS AUDITED AND FOUND TO CONTAIN NO ACCUSATION. Expecting blows and wounds, the chain finds only words of appeasement - what is my transgression, you felt all my vessels, what did you find? - and R. Simon adds the clean-hands claim that he benefited from not one vessel, not a needle, not a hook. The contrast is drawn against a later figure's plea that names bloodshed. The heading is stated as a general observation: the combativeness of the fathers, and not the humility of the sons.

check.note: A quarrel audited for its actual content and found to contain appeasement, with a clean-hands claim and a contrast case.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 74:13
claim_en: A KINSHIP CLAIM IS DERIVED FROM TWO DOUBLED PHRASES. From the doubling in 'my daughters and to my daughters', and from the pair of clauses at 31:50, the conclusion is drawn that all four mothers were the same man's daughters - the two handmaids included. The sons are separately read into the word 'brethren' when he tells them to gather stones, on the ground that the sacred tongue can call them so: mighty like him, righteous like him.

check.note: A kinship claim about four figures derived from two doubled phrases in the antagonist's own speech.

middah: E10 (my-daughters doubled and the two clauses of 31:50 — all four mothers his daughters)

claim_en: THE AFFLICTION TOKEN'S FAR CAREER. Marital deprivation is called AFFLICTION from this unit's own oath clause — 'if you afflict my daughters' — the recorded source of the Yom Kippur affliction roster's fifth member: the afflict-ban this unit filed as oath-content at derivation turns out to carry a Day of Atonement law. Filed F-121, auto-seated (round 32, the betrothal block).
middah: I2 (affliction is marital deprivation from if-you-afflict-my-daughters — the Yom Kippur roster's fifth; Yoma 77a)

source: Bava Kamma 65b:17-18
claim_en: THE DAY-OLD RAM. A day-old ram is called ram — for if 'rams' meant only the grown, Jacob's protest would imply he ate the lambs: the sacrificial age-word defined by the protest clause. Filed F-160, auto-seated (round 37, the table-and-knife block).
middah: M-09 (a day-old ram is called ram — the age-word defined by the protest clause; Bava Kamma 65b)

source: Bava Metzia 93b:3
claim_en: THE PAID KEEPER'S CEILING. Guard as far as by-day-the-heat-consumed-me-and-frost-by-night — Jacob's protest as the care standard, the extra-guarding answer recorded. Filed F-186, auto-seated (round 40, the conduct block).
middah: plain (the paid keeper's ceiling from Jacob's heat-and-frost protest — Bava Metzia 93b)
